key_claims.claim: Migratory birds navigate using a quantum compass based on entangled electron spins in cryptochrome proteins
key_claims.evidence_strength: Moderate — in vitro magnetic sensitivity confirmed; in vivo entanglement not directly measured
key_claims.falsifiability: High — mutagenesis of Cry4, RF field disruption, wavelength dependence all testable

key_claims.claim: Cryptochrome 4a (Cry4a) is the primary magnetoreceptor protein in avian retina
key_claims.evidence_strength: Strong — expression pattern, in vitro magnetic sensitivity, genetic knockout behavioral effects
key_claims.falsifiability: High — Cry4a knockout should abolish magnetic orientation

key_claims.claim: The radical pair mechanism operates through 'live' non-equilibrium quantum sensing maintained by metabolic driving
key_claims.evidence_strength: Weak-to-Moderate — theoretical framework (Smith 2026); no direct biological validation yet
key_claims.falsifiability: Moderate — requires measurement of driven radical motion in vivo

key_claims.claim: A hybrid radical-pair + magnetite mechanism amplifies the magnetic field 60–120× at the receptor site
key_claims.evidence_strength: Weak — theoretical model (PNAS 2026); no magnetite receptor identified in birds
key_claims.falsifiability: High — predicts specific magnetite nanoparticle sizes (R > 35 nm) and spatial colocalization with Cry4a

recent_literature_2024_2026.citation: Smith et al., J. Phys. Chem. Lett., 2026
recent_literature_2024_2026.key_finding: Driven radical motion (harmonic oscillation of inter-radical distance) vastly amplifies magnetic sensitivity via LZSM transitions; introduces 'live quantum sensing' framework linking entanglement to metabolic non-equilibrium
recent_literature_2024_2026.relevance: Theoretical refinement — entanglement language maintained but reframed as dynamically controlled, persistent phenomenon

recent_literature_2024_2026.citation: Zou et al., Commun. Comput. Chem., 2025
recent_literature_2024_2026.key_finding: Comprehensive review confirming Cry4 as leading candidate; notes 'direct evidence is still lacking' for in vivo operation; thermal motion at 40–43°C is major coherence threat
recent_literature_2024_2026.relevance: Status assessment — plausible but unproven in vivo

recent_literature_2024_2026.key_finding: Proposes radical pairs + magnetite nanoparticles work together; magnetite crystals >35 nm radius amplify local field 60–120×, solving the sensitivity problem
recent_literature_2024_2026.relevance: Paradigm shift — if confirmed, entanglement is assisted by classical magnetite, not operating alone

recent_literature_2024_2026.key_finding: Cry4a W369F mutant shows increased magnetic sensitivity in vitro; nature optimized for signaling (4 Trps) at expense of raw sensitivity; 'new gold standard' for biologically relevant spectroscopy
recent_literature_2024_2026.relevance: Experimental progress — in vitro sensitivity improving, but still not at physiological temperature in vivo

recent_literature_2024_2026.key_finding: Reviews cryptochrome in vitro sensitivity; notes effects start at 'tens of mT' — far above Earth's ~50 μT; gap between in vitro and in vivo remains
recent_literature_2024_2026.relevance: Persistent challenge — the sensitivity gap is the central unresolved problem
